newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Afghanistan's Taleban claim take town north of Kabul.
newsitem.headline: Afghanistan's Taleban claim take town north of Kabul.

text.p: Forces of the purist Islamic Taleban on Thursday took a small town north of the Afghan capital Kabul, according to a senior Taleban official in Kabul.

"We have taken the town of Gul Dara (19 miles or 30 km north of Kabul) and we have surrounded the opposition in Mir Batcha Kot (17 miles or 27 km from Kabul)," said Mullah Khairullah Khairkhwa, the Taleban Interior Minister, on Thursday afternoon.
A front line commander said on Thursday morning that there had been fierce fighting on Wednesday night and early on Thursday morning.

Mullah Abdul Manan said earlier Mir Bacha Kot had been taken by Taleban forces but remained under heavy fire. There was no independent confirmation of his comments and Manan would not allow journalists to visit the areas he said had been captured, saying that the area was still too dangerous.
The sound of heavy artillery barrages and rocket fire was clearly audible in Kabul itself on Wednesday night and into the early hours of Thursday morning.
Manan said that the Taleban had advanced after an opposition attack.
"They (the opposition) launched an offensive last night and again this morning, after they were exhausted the Taleban forces pushed forward," said Manan.
Taleban fighters said that an opposition plane had bombed a village north of Kabul, killing as many as four people and wounding five.

"A plane came over at 10.30 this morning (0600 GMT) and dropped a bomb on a village. We think that four people were killed, but the relatives are still digging through the rubble. We treated five people for wounds." said Taleban commander Mullah Tabibullah, commander of a checkpoint that doubles as a first aid post.
There were bloodstains and used syringes in the dust beside the road.

The opposition moved southwards towards Kabul in a rapid advance in which the Taleban were pushed back from the Hindu Kush mountains to within 15 miles (24 km) of Kabul. The advance put the opposition within rocketing range of the Afghan capital for the first time in nine months.

If the Taleban claims of an advance are confirmed, Thursday's action will be the first time that the front lines on the two main roads leading north from Kabul have changed since the opposition advance.

The capture of Gul Dara tightens the net around a salient of opposition territory. Gul Dara is on the western side of the opposition-held area; on Tuesday the Taleban took some high ground to the east of the opposition.

Thursday's action comes on the same day as the opposition postponed a meeting with the United Nations special envoy to Afghanistan, Norbert Holl. Holl was supposed to meet opposition leaders in their stronghold of Mazar-i-Sharif in northern Afghanistan on Thursday.

U.N. officials in the town said that the meeting was postponed because General Abdul Malik, one of the leaders of the tripartite oppositon alliance and a representative of Ahmed Shah Masood, another of the leaders, could not be in Mazar on Thursday.
"We have been told that General Abdul Malik and a delegate representing Masood cannot be in Mazar on Thursday, the talks have been rescheduled for Friday," said the officials.
